verdicts.name: Cross-sectional momentum among coins (1-4 week formation, 1-week hold)
verdicts.note: Direction of the verdict (weak, decayed, survivorship-inflated) is right, but the supporting 'clean 2020-2026 test on 25 liquid coins' is NOT clean: I opened github.com/prams2104/crypto-momentum-backtest and the README lists the 25 coins with no selection methodology; the list includes SOL, AVAX, NEAR, APT, ICP, SHIB, which did not exist or were not listed on Binance in Jan 2020, so the universe is hand-picked from 2025 survivors (look-ahead/survivorship), single-author, unreviewed, 20-day lookback only, 20 bps one-way cost is the author's assumption. Its Sharpe path 0.42 -> -0.48 -> -2.18 and the 38% dispersion drop (3.20% -> 1.98%) are confirmed as reported, but they are anecdotal, not a replication. Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (JF 2022, 1,827 coins, 2014-2020) does document a significant 1-4 week momentum factor in-sample; the specific '11.2%/wk top quintile' and 'Sharpe 0.48' figures could not be confirmed (Wiley/NBER blocked). Ammann et al. survivorship numbers (62.19%/yr EW, 0.93% VW) and Fieberg et al. -255% crash could not be opened (SSRN/Springer blocked); Grobys & Shahzad IJFE 2026 and CTREND 3.87%/wk likewise unverified. Keep as weak; treat every quoted number as second-hand.

verdicts.name: Time-series momentum (TSMOM) on BTC/ETH/coin-market index, 1-4 week lookback
verdicts.note: Liu & Tsyvinski (RFS 2021) do report that 1-week coin-market returns predict returns 1-4 weeks ahead (in-sample, 2011-2018, no OOS test) - qualitatively holds. But the three post-2020 sources carrying the 'moderate' rating are all unreviewed and unopened: the Zenodo pre/post-ETF study (Sharpe 0.82 -> 1.22), the Vilnius 8-coin comparison (31.96% ann.) and the summitward.com blog (Sharpe 0.74 vs 0.79). None is peer-reviewed, none could be fetched, none reports costs in a way I could check. No peer-reviewed post-2022 crypto TSMOM replication with costs is known to me either. Downgrade to weak-to-moderate: the robust content is drawdown reduction from vol targeting, not the direction call.

verdicts.name: Multi-lookback Donchian breakout ensemble with volatility targeting (long-only trend)
verdicts.note: Confirmed second-hand via two independent GitHub replication notes (alfred1123/Quant_Strategies PR 61; zebadee2kk/DeFi-TraderStack-Agent issue 137): BTC CAGR 30%, vol 17%, Sharpe 1.56, MDD 19%; ETH 27%/16%/1.51/15%; BNB 17%/15%/1.06/17%, all net of 10 bps; top-20 rotational Sharpe 1.58, Sortino 2.03, alpha +14% vs BTC net of 0.10-0.50%. The replications also confirm internal inconsistencies (combination MAR reported as both 0.88 and 1.15; Sortino 2.03 vs 1.23; '34%' vs 36% CAGR) and several [UNSTATED] parameters (universe membership rules beyond $2M median volume, exact trailing-stop mechanics, leverage). SSRN itself was blocked. Single in-sample backtest, no holdout, working paper - 'moderate' is generous; moderate-minus.

verdicts.name: Moving-average rules on Bitcoin (5-100 day MA, VMA crossovers)
verdicts.note: Detzel et al. (Financial Management 2021) do report in- and out-of-sample predictability from price-to-MA ratios on BTC 2011-2018 - qualitative claim holds from memory, but the quoted '11-58x larger returns on long-signal days' and 'Sharpe +0.2-0.6' could not be verified (Wiley blocked). The Hudson & Urquhart citation is mis-specified: their large-scale study ('Technical trading and cryptocurrencies') is in Annals of Operations Research (2021) and tests ~15,000 rules on BTC/ETH/LTC/XRP, not '2,127 rules' in FRL 2019; the FRL 2019 link is more likely Corbet et al. or Grobys et al. The 'zero OOS predictability for Bitcoin' claim could not be confirmed against the actual paper. 'Weak' is the right rating; the source attributions need fixing.

verdicts.name: Short-term (1-day / 1-week) cross-sectional reversal
verdicts.note: Zaremba et al. (IRFA 2021) result - reversal concentrated in small illiquid coins, largest coins show short-term continuation - matches my knowledge of the paper. Kosc-Sakowski-Slepaczuk (Physica A 2019) contrarian dominance on 2015-2017 also matches. GitHub 1-day reversal numbers confirmed from README: OOS 2025-26 gross alpha +73% (t=4.64) but net Sharpe -1.73 and '+73% gross -> -29% net' at 20 bps with 138-139% daily turnover; note the training-period reversal was NEGATIVE gross (alpha -5.5%, Sharpe -3.21), so even the sign is unstable across subperiods. Same survivorship caveat on the 25-coin universe applies. Weak is correct.

verdicts.name: Longer-run reversal (>1 month) among coins
verdicts.note: Dobrynskaya (SSRN 2021, 'Cryptocurrency momentum and reversal') does report momentum up to ~4 weeks then reversal, on ~2,000 coins 2014-2020 - consistent with memory, but SSRN is blocked so effect sizes and the 'loser-driven' claim are unconfirmed; the FRL 2025 behavioural-reversal paper is unknown to me. Unreviewed, pre-2021 sample, likely survivorship-contaminated. Keep weak, flag as unverified.

verdicts.name: 15-minute sign reversal (short-horizon mean reversion)
verdicts.note: arXiv 2608.21888 is dated August 2026, after my knowledge cutoff, and arxiv.org is blocked; I cannot confirm the 183 pairs / 90% / 2-3 AUC-point figures, the OOS protocol, or even the paper's existence. Downgrade from moderate to unverifiable/weak until someone opens the PDF. Note also that 2-3 AUC points at 15 min is below round-trip costs on any venue the owner can use, so even if true it is a feature, not a signal.

verdicts.name: Quarter-hour / turn-of-the-candle periodicity and order-imbalance at clock marks
verdicts.note: Kim & Hansen (arXiv 2607.09426, July 2026) is after my cutoff and blocked; the order-imbalance -> 4-12h forecast claim, the funding-hour robustness check and the 'Kimbrough replication' cannot be confirmed. Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough (JFEc 2024) periodicity in volatility/volume is a real, peer-reviewed result and holds. Turn-of-the-candle (Heliyon 2023, arXiv 2109.12142) I recall as a real paper on BTC candle-boundary minute returns, but the '0.58 bps/min, t>9 on seven exchanges' figures are unconfirmed. Downgrade to weak/unverifiable; the only tradable piece (OI at quarter-hour marks) rests on one unverified preprint.

verdicts.name: Hour-of-day / overnight (US-off-hours) seasonality in BTC
verdicts.note: Rated weak, which is right. Quantpedia's intraday-seasonality write-up (Gemini BTC, 21:00-23:00 UTC window) exists but is a vendor backtest with no holdout, found by scanning 24 hours; numbers (33% ann., 20.9% vol, -22.5% MDD) could not be re-checked (blocked). Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough JFEc 2024 finding periodicity in vol/volume not returns is peer-reviewed and consistent with memory.

verdicts.name: Day-of-week / weekend effect
verdicts.note: 'No-evidence' is correct. Sources are a Substack post, MDPI and a low-tier journal; sign flips across subperiods are exactly what one expects from a null effect plus multiple testing. Nothing to upgrade; nothing could be opened.

verdicts.name: Intraday time-series momentum (first-half-hour -> last-half-hour) in BTC
verdicts.note: Wen, Bouri, Xu, Zhao (NAJEF 2022, 'Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: momentum, reversal, or both') is a real peer-reviewed paper reporting both momentum and reversal patterns conditioned on jumps/liquidity/COVID, sample to 2020. Coefficients not verifiable (ScienceDirect blocked). 'Weak' is appropriate; the 24/7 market has no natural open/close so the effect is a US-session artefact.

verdicts.name: Volatility scaling / volatility-managed trend and momentum (risk-management overlay)
verdicts.note: The qualitative finding is robust and well replicated across asset classes (Kim-Tse-Wald JFM 2016; Moreira-Muir 2017; Barroso-Santa-Clara 2015 for momentum crashes), so 'strong' as a risk overlay is defensible. But two of the four supporting numbers are unverified: the exact 1.27% vs 0.41% alpha split could not be checked (ScienceDirect blocked; my recollection is only that unscaled TSMOM alpha is much smaller and often insignificant), and the crypto-specific 0.74 vs 0.79 Sharpe comparison comes from an unreviewed blog (summitward.com) that could not be opened. Fieberg et al. 3.47% vs 3.18%/wk unverified (Springer blocked). Keep strong for 'improves risk-adjusted returns / cuts drawdowns'; it says nothing about directional accuracy, and the summary should not imply it does.

verdicts.name: Hourly ML direction forecasts from technical (momentum/MA/RSI) features
verdicts.note: arXiv 2606.00060 (Bysik & Slepaczuk, June 2026) is at the edge of my cutoff and blocked; I cannot confirm the 27-fold walk-forward design, the '>65% ann. return, Sharpe >1' configuration, or the bootstrap non-dominance result. The Slepaczuk group's earlier crypto ML papers consistently find that naive hourly sign strategies die at ~10 bps, so the qualitative claim is plausible. Weak/unverifiable.

corrected.family: Price-based: time-series momentum, trend, reversal, cross-sectional momentum, intraday seasonality (crypto)
corrected.summary: Referee's bottom line (verification status: only github.com was reachable in this session; publisher/arXiv/SSRN/NBER/Semantic Scholar domains are egress-blocked and the WebSearch budget was already exhausted, so most numbers below are cross-checked against my own knowledge of the papers and flagged when I could not confirm them). What survives scrutiny: (1) volatility targeting / vol-managed sizing is the one component with strong, multi-decade, multi-asset, peer-reviewed support - but it improves Sharpe and drawdowns, not directional hit rate; (2) slow multi-lookback trend/breakout on BTC/ETH/top-20 liquid coins (Zarattini et al. 2025 Donchian ensemble; Detzel et al. 2021 MA ratios; Liu-Tsyvinski 2021 1-4 week TSMOM) has consistent in-sample support and two third-party GitHub replications confirm the Zarattini headline numbers (BTC Sharpe 1.56, CAGR 30%, MDD 19% net of 10 bps) while also confirming internal inconsistencies and unstated parameters - rate moderate-minus, no formal holdout, no peer review; (3) cross-sectional short-term reversal exists but is a small-coin liquidity artefact; in large coins the sign is continuation, and net of 20 bps a 1-day reversal on liquid coins loses money (+73% gross alpha -> about -29% net, 138% daily turnover, confirmed from the repo README). What does NOT hold or cannot be verified: cross-sectional 1-4 week momentum is in-sample (2014-2020), survivorship-inflated, crash-prone and appears to have decayed post-2022 - but the widely quoted 'clean point-in-time 2020-2026 test' is not clean (its 25-coin universe includes SOL, AVAX, NEAR, APT, ICP, SHIB, which did not exist in Jan 2020, i.e. it is a 2025 survivor list), so treat the decay evidence as suggestive, not a replication. The three 2026 arXiv preprints carrying the intraday claims (15-min sign reversal, quarter-hour order imbalance, hourly ML with cost filter) are all after my knowledge cutoff and could not be opened: downgrade all three to unverifiable. Calendar/hour-of-day effects remain no-evidence-to-weak. Realistic expectation for the advisor: daily-horizon directional hit rates of 51-55% on BTC/ETH from trend features, most of the economic value from vol-scaled sizing and drawdown control, and every sub-daily edge below realistic Telegram-latency execution costs. No source promises returns; several document post-publication decay. Every number tagged '[unverified]' must be re-derived from the owner's own point-in-time data before being used as a model prior.

predictors.name: Cross-sectional momentum among coins (1-4 week formation, 1-week hold)
predictors.formula: Each week rank coins by r_{t-k,t} for k in {1,2,3,4} weeks (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu: cap > $1M, value-weighted quintiles); long top quintile, short bottom quintile, hold 1 week. CTREND variant (Fieberg et al. JFQA 2024): rolling cross-sectional regression of next-week return on a set of moving-average/price-trend indicators; fitted value = signal.
predictors.universe_period: Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu JF 2022: 1,827 coins, Jan 2014-Jul 2020 (in-sample). Ammann et al. SSRN 4287573: ~3,900 coins 2014-2021 [unverified]. Fieberg et al. FMPM 2025: top-30 coins weekly 2016-2023 [unverified]. prams2104 GitHub test: 25 coins, 1 Jan 2020-5 Feb 2026, train 2020-22 / val 2023-24 / OOS 2025-26 - universe is a 2025 survivor list, NOT point-in-time.
predictors.effect: In-sample (JF 2022): significant 1-4 week momentum factor; the '~3%/wk long-short', '11.2%/wk top quintile' and 'Sharpe 0.48' figures could not be verified this session. CTREND 3.87%/wk [unverified]. Fieberg et al. -255% single-coin crash in 2022 [unverified]. Grobys & Shahzad infinite-variance claim [unverified]. GitHub 20-day momentum at 20 bps one-way (confirmed from README): net Sharpe 0.42 / alpha 36.2% (t=2.02) train; -0.48 / 13.5% (t=1.08) val; -2.18 / -12.5% (t=-0.81) OOS; cross-sectional dispersion 3.20% pre-2023 vs 1.98% post-2023 (-38%).
predictors.oos_evidence: Weak to negative. No peer-reviewed post-2022 replication with costs and a point-in-time universe is known to me. The GitHub decay evidence is directionally informative but survivorship-contaminated (universe chosen ex post) and single-lookback. Ammann et al. survivorship finding (momentum premium disappears after delisting control) is plausible and consistent with the equity/crypto literature but unverified here.
predictors.costs_decay: Weekly long-short quintile rebalance in alts implies 100-200% weekly turnover; at 10-30 bps taker+spread plus perp funding on shorts the in-sample premium shrinks materially. Post-2021 dispersion collapse is the most credible decay mechanism. Use only as a regime-conditional feature (dispersion-gated), never standalone.
predictors.data_source: Daily OHLCV + market cap for a POINT-IN-TIME universe including delisted coins (CoinGecko/CMC historical snapshots, Binance listing/delisting dates); tradable subset via ccxt Binance/OKX perps. Rebuild the universe monthly from listing dates, not from today's top-N.

predictors.name: Time-series momentum (TSMOM) on BTC/ETH/coin-market index, 1-4 week lookback
predictors.formula: signal_t = sign(r_{t-k,t}), k = 1..4 weeks (Liu-Tsyvinski) or 12 months (MOP 2012); position = signal * sigma_target / sigma_hat_t, sigma_hat = 20-90d realized vol, leverage cap 1x for long-only. Alternative: EWMA-difference (fast minus slow EMA) normalized by vol.
predictors.universe_period: Liu & Tsyvinski RFS 2021: value-weighted coin-market index 2011-2018 (in-sample predictive regressions, peer-reviewed). Post-ETF study (Zenodo, 2018-Mar 2026), Vilnius 8-coin study (2020-Oct 2025), summitward BTC/ETH/SOL (2017-mid 2025): all unreviewed and unopened.
predictors.effect: RFS 2021: one-week market return positively and significantly predicts the next 1-4 week returns (in-sample). Post-2020 magnitudes quoted in the prior draft (Sharpe 0.82 -> 1.22 post-ETF; 31.96% ann.; vol-managed 0.74 vs trend 0.79) are ALL [unverified, unreviewed].
predictors.oos_evidence: No peer-reviewed post-2022 OOS replication with costs known. Directionally the effect persists in trending years (2020-21, 2023-24) and whipsaws in 2022-type chop; the return contribution beyond vol scaling is small and fragile (cf. Kim-Tse-Wald 2016 decomposition on futures).
predictors.costs_decay: Low turnover, 5-10 bps tolerable on BTC/ETH. Expect flat-to-negative in range-bound regimes. Always benchmark against a vol-managed long-only position, not buy-and-hold.
predictors.data_source: Daily OHLCV BTC/ETH/large alts via ccxt (Binance/Coinbase/Kraken); realized vol from daily returns; optional VW coin-market index from CoinGecko.

predictors.name: Multi-lookback Donchian breakout ensemble with volatility targeting (long-only trend)
predictors.formula: For L in {5,10,20,30,60,90,150,250,360} days: long when close > max(close, L); exit on trailing stop = max(prior stop, (channel max+min)/2); ensemble = equal-weighted average of sub-strategy positions; size = 0.25 / sigma_90d (25% ann. vol target), leverage cap 1x, daily rebalance with a 20% rebalance threshold. Trailing-stop mechanics and universe membership rules are partly [UNSTATED] in the paper per replicators.
predictors.universe_period: BTC Jan 2015-Mar 2025; ETH from Aug 2015; BNB from Jul 2017; rotational top-20 liquid coins (>=1 yr listed, median 30d volume >= $2M), monthly membership. SSRN working paper, not peer-reviewed.
predictors.effect: Confirmed second-hand from two independent GitHub replication notes: BTC net of 10 bps CAGR 30%, vol 17%, Sharpe 1.56, MDD 19%; ETH 27% / 16% / 1.51 / 15%; BNB 17% / 15% / 1.06 / 17%; top-20 rotational Sharpe 1.58, Sortino 2.03, alpha +14%/yr vs BTC net of 0.10-0.50% per trade. Replicators note vol weights never exceed 1x on Binance spot (median raw weight 0.32-0.43).
predictors.oos_evidence: None formal - single 2015-2025 in-sample backtest. Replications flag internal inconsistencies (combination MAR 0.88 vs 1.15; Sortino 2.03 vs 1.23; CAGR '34%' vs 36%). Ensemble of 9 lookbacks and a point-in-time universe reduce but do not remove selection risk; post-Mar-2025 performance unknown.
predictors.costs_decay: Tested net of 10-50 bps; vol-scaling churn needs rebalance bands. Long-only, so bear years are flat by construction. Post-publication decay unknown (published Apr 2025).
predictors.data_source: Daily OHLC for BTC/ETH/top-20 liquid coins via ccxt (Kraken/Binance); historical volume for the liquidity filter; listing/delisting dates for the rotational universe.

predictors.name: Moving-average rules on Bitcoin (price-to-MA ratios, VMA crossovers)
predictors.formula: Detzel et al.: signal_t = 1{P_t > MA_L} for L in 1-20 weeks (also multi-MA combinations); hold BTC if 1 else cash; predictive regression r_{t+1} = a + b*log(P_t/MA_L) + e with in- and out-of-sample R2. VMA: buy when short MA (1-5d) > long MA (50-200d) by a band.
predictors.universe_period: Detzel et al. Financial Management 2021: BTC 2011-2018. Grobys-Ahmed-Sapkota FRL 2020: 11 cryptos 2016-2018. Hudson & Urquhart: ~15,000 rules on BTC/ETH/LTC/XRP with data-snooping corrections (Annals of Operations Research 2021 - venue/rule-count in the prior draft was wrong).
predictors.effect: Detzel: price-to-MA ratios predict BTC returns in- and out-of-sample and MA strategies raise Sharpe and cut drawdowns (peer-reviewed); the specific '11-58x' and '+0.2-0.6 Sharpe' figures are [unverified]. Hudson & Urquhart: some rules survive reality-check in-sample; the claim of zero OOS predictability for BTC is [unverified]. Retail 50/200 crossover backtests: drawdown reduction, no total-return edge.
predictors.oos_evidence: Contradictory between studies; consistent with MA distance being a slow trend/drawdown filter rather than a directional edge. Sullivan-Timmermann-White (1999) show best-of-many rules do not repeat OOS.
predictors.costs_decay: Short MAs cost-sensitive at 10+ bps; long MAs trade rarely. Use log(P/MA_L) for several L as continuous features; never select one 'best' rule.
predictors.data_source: Daily close BTC/ETH via ccxt.

predictors.name: Short-term (1-day / 1-week) cross-sectional reversal
predictors.formula: Rank coins by prior 1-day (or 1-week) return; long bottom decile/quintile, short top; hold 1 day (1 week).
predictors.universe_period: Zaremba et al. IRFA 2021: >3,600 coins 2015-2021. Kosc-Sakowski-Slepaczuk Physica A 2019: top-100 coins 2015-2017. GitHub test: 25 (survivor-selected) liquid coins 2020-2026.
predictors.effect: Zaremba et al.: reversal is driven by small illiquid coins; the largest coins (~90% of cap) show short-term CONTINUATION - consistent with the paper as I know it. GitHub 1-day reversal at 20 bps one-way (confirmed): train Sharpe -3.21 / gross alpha -5.5%; val -4.51 / +17.1% (t=1.37); OOS 2025-26 -1.73 / +73.0% (t=4.64), turnover 138-139%/day, i.e. +73% gross -> about -29% net. Note the training-period sign was negative, so even the gross effect is unstable.
predictors.oos_evidence: Small-coin reversal is bid-ask bounce, not tradable. On liquid coins the sign flips across subperiods and net-of-cost results are negative.
predictors.costs_decay: Dies above ~5 bps round trip at daily rebalance. For BTC/ETH the relevant (small) fact is daily continuation.
predictors.data_source: Daily close/volume/cap for a point-in-time universe; tradable version on Binance perps via ccxt.

predictors.name: Longer-run reversal (>1 month) among coins
predictors.formula: Sort coins on past J-week return, J >= 4-8 weeks; long losers, short winners; hold K >= 4 weeks.
predictors.effect: Momentum up to ~4 weeks, then reversal beyond ~1 month, 'economically large' [unverified].
predictors.oos_evidence: None known post-2020; loser-driven reversal in a 2014-2020 sample is exposed to survivorship (dead losers) and to 2017-18 boom/bust episodes.
predictors.costs_decay: Cheap turnover but the loser leg is illiquid with delisting risk; likely decayed post-2021.
predictors.data_source: Weekly prices/caps for a point-in-time universe incl. delisted coins.

predictors.name: 15-minute sign reversal (short-horizon mean reversion)
predictors.formula: Predict sign(r_{t+1}) at 15-min bars as -sign(r_t); scored by AUC under an out-of-sample protocol (per the preprint's abstract as summarised in the prior draft).
predictors.universe_period: Claimed: 183 Binance pairs vs 187 US stocks/ETFs, 2021-2026. arXiv 2608.21888 (Aug 2026) - after my knowledge cutoff and unreachable; existence and numbers unconfirmed.
predictors.effect: Claimed 90% of pairs significant, 2-3 AUC points (~52-53% sign hit rate) [unverified].
predictors.oos_evidence: Cannot be assessed. Even if true, the edge is below round-trip costs at 15-min cadence.
predictors.costs_decay: At 15-min rebalance, 2 bps maker fees roughly equal the claimed edge per bar; only usable as an entry-timing feature.
predictors.data_source: Binance 15-min klines via ccxt.

predictors.name: Quarter-hour / turn-of-the-candle periodicity and order-imbalance at clock marks
predictors.formula: Turn-of-candle: mean return in minutes {0,15,30,45} vs other minutes. Order-imbalance: OI = (buy - sell volume)/(total) in the opening seconds of each quarter-hour; regress subsequent 4-12h returns on OI.
predictors.universe_period: Turn-of-candle: BTC on multiple exchanges, effect from ~2020 (Heliyon 2023 / arXiv 2109.12142) [numbers unverified]. Kim & Hansen arXiv 2607.09426 (Jul 2026, BTC/ETH/XRP/SOL/DOGE/ADA Binance perps 2021-2024) - after cutoff, unreachable.
predictors.effect: Claimed 0.58 bps/min at candle turns with t>9 [unverified]; claimed OI at quarter-hour marks forecasts 4-12h returns OOS [unverified]. Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough JFEc 2024 (peer-reviewed): strong periodicity in volatility and volume, improving GARCH forecasts OOS - this part holds.
predictors.oos_evidence: Only the volatility/volume periodicity is peer-reviewed. Return-forecasting claims rest on unverified preprints and on an adaptive phenomenon that appeared in 2020 and can vanish.
predictors.costs_decay: Per-minute edge below taker fees; the OI -> hours forecast would be the only tradable piece and is unconfirmed.
predictors.data_source: Binance futures aggTrades and 1-min klines (ccxt fetch_trades / Binance data portal).

predictors.name: Hour-of-day / overnight (US-off-hours) seasonality in BTC
predictors.formula: Hold BTC only in a fixed UTC window (e.g. 21:00-23:00 UTC) or overnight vs NYSE-session split.
predictors.universe_period: Quantpedia (Gemini BTC ~2015-2022), paperswithbacktest extension; no peer-reviewed source. Unopened.
predictors.effect: Claimed ~33% ann., 20.9% vol, -22.5% MDD for the 21:00-23:00 window [unverified]; found by scanning 24 hourly windows.
predictors.oos_evidence: No holdout; multiple-testing artefact risk. Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough 2024: periodicity in vol/volume, not in expected returns.
predictors.costs_decay: Two round trips per day; use session dummies as volatility/liquidity features only.
predictors.data_source: Hourly BTC/ETH klines via ccxt; NYSE calendar.

predictors.name: Day-of-week / weekend effect
predictors.formula: r_t = sum_d b_d D_d + e on daily/hourly returns.
predictors.universe_period: BTC daily 2014-2024 and multi-coin COVID-era samples (Substack, MDPI, low-tier journals).
predictors.effect: No stable return gap; sign flips across subperiods; lower weekend volume/volatility.
predictors.oos_evidence: None; consistent with null plus multiple testing.
predictors.costs_decay: Not a signal; weekday/weekend dummies only as liquidity features for sizing.
predictors.data_source: Daily/hourly BTC/ETH via ccxt.

predictors.name: Intraday time-series momentum (first-half-hour -> last-half-hour) in BTC
predictors.formula: r_last30 = a + b * r_first30 + e per UTC/exchange day; timing strategy takes sign(r_first30) in the last half hour.
predictors.universe_period: Wen-Bouri-Xu-Zhao NAJEF 2022: BTC HF data 2013-2020 (peer-reviewed); coefficients unverified.
predictors.effect: Both momentum and reversal, conditional on jumps, FOMC, liquidity, COVID; claimed utility gain over buy-and-hold [unverified].
predictors.oos_evidence: Paper reports OOS economic-value comparisons; no post-2020 replication; effect is a US-session artefact overlapping hour-of-day seasonality.
predictors.costs_decay: One round trip per day affordable at ~5 bps but the effect is small and conditional.
predictors.data_source: 1-5 min BTC/ETH klines via ccxt; FOMC calendar; jump detection.

predictors.name: Volatility scaling / volatility-managed trend and momentum (risk-management overlay)
predictors.formula: w_t = signal_t * sigma_target / sigma_hat_t, sigma_hat = 20-90d realized or EWMA vol; cap at 1x long-only. Risk-managed WML: WML * c / sigma_WML,t.
predictors.universe_period: Kim-Tse-Wald JFM 2016 (58 futures 1965-2009); Moreira-Muir JF 2017; Barroso-Santa-Clara JFE 2015 (equity momentum crashes); Fieberg et al. FMPM 2025 crypto [unverified]; summitward BTC/ETH/SOL 2017-2025 [unreviewed, unverified].
predictors.effect: Peer-reviewed, multi-asset: most of MOP's TSMOM alpha comes from vol scaling (exact 1.27% vs 0.41% split unverified); vol management sharply reduces momentum crashes. Crypto-specific Sharpe 0.74 (vol-managed, no signal) vs 0.79 (with trend) is from a blog and unverified.
predictors.oos_evidence: Consistent across decades and asset classes; a property of vol clustering, which persists. Improves risk-adjusted return and drawdowns; does NOT raise directional accuracy.
predictors.costs_decay: Resizing churn; use rebalance bands (10-20% weight change). No evidence of decay.
predictors.data_source: Daily returns of traded assets.

predictors.name: Hourly ML direction forecasts from technical features with cost-aware trade filter
predictors.formula: XGBoost/LSTM/iTransformer on lagged returns + TA indicators predicting next-hour BTC-USDT return; trade only if |forecast| > cost threshold; walk-forward folds.
predictors.universe_period: BTC-USDT hourly 2018-2026, arXiv 2606.00060 (Jun 2026) - at/after my cutoff, unreachable.
predictors.effect: Claimed positive gross in selected configs, naive sign-following fails at 10 bps, best long-only XGBoost >65% ann. / Sharpe >1 with cost filter, no bootstrap dominance [unverified]. Directional accuracy ~50%.
predictors.oos_evidence: Claimed walk-forward; 'selected configurations' implies configuration search; not replicated.
predictors.costs_decay: Any hourly Telegram signal must be gated by a cost/magnitude threshold.
predictors.data_source: Hourly BTC/ETH klines via ccxt.

predictors.name: [ADDED] 12-month time-series momentum / 52-week-high proximity on BTC/ETH

Source mis-attribution in the prior draft: the large-scale data-snooping study by Hudson & Urquhart is in Annals of Operations Research (2021) with ~15,000 rules, not FRL 2019 with 2,127 rules; the FRL 2019 links are other papers. The 'zero OOS predictability for Bitcoin' claim is unverified.

Survivorship/delisting bias dominates crypto cross-sectional results (Ammann et al., unverified magnitude); any universe built from today's top-N is invalid. Rebuild universes monthly from listing dates including delisted coins.

Infinite-variance / single-coin-crash risk in long-short crypto momentum (Grobys & Shahzad 2026; Fieberg et al. 2025 - both unverified but consistent with known short-leg blow-ups): do not rank strategies by Sharpe alone; cap per-coin exposure.

Most trend-following 'alpha' in crypto is volatility scaling; the crypto-specific decomposition (Sharpe 0.74 no-signal vs 0.79 with trend) is from an unreviewed blog, but the peer-reviewed futures decomposition (Kim-Tse-Wald 2016) supports the same conclusion. Benchmark every directional signal against a vol-managed long-only position.
Transaction costs flip signs below daily horizon: 1-day reversal +73% gross -> about -29% net at 20 bps (confirmed); anything at 15-min to 1-h cadence is below Telegram-latency execution costs.
Calendar/hour-of-day/day-of-week effects are multiple-testing artefacts absent pre-registration; only volatility/volume periodicity is peer-reviewed (Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough JFEc 2024).

corrected.family: Derivatives positioning: funding, basis, open interest, liquidations, options
corrected.summary: Referee verdict after re-check (with a hard caveat: this session's egress proxy blocked every academic and vendor host - arXiv and all its mirrors, SSRN, BIS, Wiley, ScienceDirect, INFORMS, Emerald, Medium, TheBlock, CoinDesk, Deribit, Binance, CFTC - and the web-search budget was exhausted; only the two GitHub-hosted studies could be opened first-hand). What was verified: (a) the pre-registered Binance funding carry-fade study confirms a gross funding premium of +0.1525%/day, but its holdout was NEVER opened (the prior text wrongly said alpha was null 'on the sealed holdout'), and - decisive for a direction advisor - its stated PRICE mechanism was falsified: the short leg's price component is -0.0198%/day with a CI spanning zero, so high funding does not predict lower prices cross-sectionally even gross; the premium is funding cash-flow, 74% of which is eaten by 1.85x daily turnover (DSR 0.76). (b) The Deribit 25-delta risk-reversal backtest is confirmed at 58.9% on n=56 (p~0.18, R^2 0.006); its T-90 77.4% (n=31) is overlapping-window, drift-confounded and cost-free, not evidence. Everything else in the family - Fulgur 8h regression, K33 negative-funding regime win rates, BIS crypto-carry crash result, Chi et al. basis sorts, Emerald OI crash logit (OR 1.48, AUC 0.677), COT papers, liquidation-cascade replication, VRP/IV papers, quarter-hour order imbalance - is UNVERIFIED in this session; the qualitative direction of those claims matches my recollection of the literature where I know the papers, but no coefficient should be quoted from this document without reading the PDF. Net assessment: derivatives positioning carries real information about LEVERAGE, CRASH RISK and VOLATILITY, and essentially none about the SIGN of the next move at horizons under a week once costs and overlapping-sample effects are accounted for. Strengths are downgraded accordingly: basis, OI change and COT drop from moderate to weak (in-sample or pre-ETF-regime only, unreplicated, unverified here); cross-sectional funding is weak for carry and no-evidence for direction. Practical implication for the GBM/triple-barrier forecaster is unchanged in spirit but sharper: use funding-regime (30d average sign/duration), OI change, basis and DVOL/VRP as inputs to BARRIER WIDTH, sizing and crash gating, and as HMM/MS-AR TVTP covariates; do not expect standalone directional edge; treat the multi-week negative-funding regime and COT positioning as hypotheses to test in-house on point-in-time data (both are free, low-turnover, and cheap to validate with purged CPCV), not as established predictors. Never promise returns from any of these.

predictors.name: Perpetual funding rate level / extremes (time-series, single asset)
predictors.formula: F_t = 8h funding rate (Binance/Bybit/OKX; exchange average). Variants: (a) raw F_t; (b) z_t = (F_t - mean_30d)/std_30d, contrarian entry when |z|>2; (c) regime: 30-day rolling mean of F_t < 0 and consecutive-day count of negative 30d average. Contrarian hypothesis sign(E[r_{t+h}]) = -sign(F_t).
predictors.effect: UNVERIFIED (hosts blocked): 8h OLS coef -0.087, p=0.008, R^2=0.003 (Fulgur 2021); daily z-score contrarian BTC 2019-2026 'slightly positive gross, ~zero/negative after fees'; K33 negative-30d-funding regime 30-360d win rate 83-96% vs 55-70% unconditional on <10 independent episodes. Consistent with verified cross-sectional finding that funding's price channel is empty at daily horizon.
predictors.oos_evidence: None formal. 8h regression in-sample; z-score study is a single full-sample null; K33 stats descriptive with overlapping forward windows and BTC's strong unconditional drift over 2018-2025; no post-publication test. All three sources unreadable in this session.
predictors.costs_decay: Taker fees (~5-10 bp round trip) exceed implied 8h/daily edge by an order of magnitude. Regime version low-turnover but statistically underpowered. Funding compressed since 2024 (fewer extremes).
predictors.data_source: Binance fapi /fapi/v1/fundingRate (full history since 2019), Bybit/OKX public APIs, ccxt fetchFundingRateHistory, data.binance.vision bulk (all blocked from this session; collect from owner's machine/VPS).

predictors.name: Funding-rate cross-sectional carry-fade / 'funding sentiment' factor
predictors.formula: Each day rank Binance USDT perps (liquidity floor: >=30d listed, trailing-30d median $ volume >= $1M, point-in-time incl. delisted) by trailing funding; short top decile (crowded longs, pay funding), long bottom decile (crowded shorts, receive funding); dollar-neutral, daily rebalance. Return decomposed into funding component + price component.
predictors.effect: VERIFIED (GitHub README + pre-registration, training period 2021-05-15..2024-12-31, 1,322 days): gross funding premium +0.001525/day; market-neutral Sharpe +0.37 ann.; daily alpha +0.000424, 95% CI [-0.000732, +0.001593]; DSR 0.762 (fails >0.95 bar); short-leg PRICE component -0.000198/day, CI [-0.002648, +0.002206] -> price-convergence mechanism FALSIFIED; turnover 1.85x/day; measured costs (half-spreads from aggTrades) consume ~74% of gross; breakeven at ~1.34x measured cost. Holdout 2025-01..2026-06 sealed and never opened. UNVERIFIED: SSRN 6701738 (10 perps 2022-07..2026-04, purged walk-forward, linear rank-IC -0.0097 t=-1.54, GBM IC +0.0243 t=3.55, net Sharpe -3.2/-2.9); SSRN 6818558 funding-sentiment factor significant at 1% (in-sample, gross); arXiv 2510.14435 carry Sharpe collapsing to negative in 2025.
predictors.universe_period: Binance USDT-M perps above $1M/day liquidity floor (113 coins in 2021 to 682 in 2026), 2021-05..2024-12 (training); other studies 10-90 perps 2020-2026
predictors.oos_evidence: Pre-registered, survivorship-free, cost-measured study: hypothesis rejected in-sample on the price component, so no OOS test was run. The gross premium is funding carry, not return prediction. Other positive results are in-sample/gross and could not be read.
predictors.costs_decay: Killed by turnover at daily rebalance; needs all-in cost roughly 25% below measured half-spreads to break even. Even at zero cost there is no price-direction content to exploit. Carry itself reportedly decayed post-2024 (unverified).
predictors.data_source: data.binance.vision klines + fundingRate + aggTrades (incl. delisted symbols); ccxt fetchFundingRateHistory; Bybit/OKX archives

predictors.name: Futures basis / crypto carry (dated futures and perp premium)
predictors.formula: Annualized basis b_t = (F_t^T/S_t - 1)*365/(T-t) for dated futures (CME, Deribit, Binance quarterly); for perps, premium index or 3*365*avg 8h funding. Cross-section: sort by basis. Time-series: high carry -> elevated crash probability over following weeks.
predictors.effect: UNVERIFIED (BIS/INFORMS/Wiley/CFB blocked): Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov report large, time-varying carry and that high carry precedes crashes, attributed to retail leverage demand vs scarce arbitrage capital (consistent with my recollection of the abstract); Chi et al. report basis as strongest daily cross-sectional sort, insignificant monthly; CF Benchmarks basis-momentum correlations 0.50/0.54. No verified coefficient. The verified funding study shows the perp-premium price channel is empty at daily horizon, which argues against a daily-basis directional signal for perps.
predictors.oos_evidence: Crash prediction is in-sample regression; cross-sectional sorts have no cost or OOS test; no post-2022 replication found; post-ETF basis compression reported (unverified).
predictors.costs_decay: Daily sorts: high turnover, same fate as funding fade. Crash gating: low turnover. CME basis arbitraged by ETF basis funds since 2024.
predictors.data_source: CME via CF Benchmarks basis indices, Coin Metrics, CryptoQuant CME basis, Deribit/Binance quarterly futures via ccxt, Kaiko

predictors.name: Open interest change (OI x price quadrant, leverage build-up)
predictors.formula: dOI_t = ln(OI_t/OI_{t-k}), k = 1h/1d/7d, USD or coin terms; leverage ratio = OI/exchange reserves or OI/market cap; quadrant = sign(dOI) x sign(dP). Crash logit P(crash_{t+1}) = f(dOI_BTC, funding, liquidations).

predictors.name: CME weekend gap fill
predictors.formula: Gap_t = CME Friday settlement - Sunday open; fade toward gap.
predictors.effect: Vendor fill-rate statistics (77%/92%) without benchmark against unconditional revisit probability; unverified and uninterpretable.
predictors.oos_evidence: None; claim that CME went gap-free in 2026 also unverified.
predictors.costs_decay: Unbounded holding period; no stop; mechanism may have ended.
predictors.data_source: CME settlements (Barchart), spot via ccxt

predictors.name: [ADDED] Taker buy/sell volume ratio and signed order-flow imbalance on perps
predictors.formula: TBR_t = taker buy volume / taker sell volume per 5m-1h bucket (Binance takerlongshortRatio, OKX taker-volume); OFI_t = sum of signed aggressive volume (aggTrades isBuyerMaker) normalized by total volume; z-scored over 24h. Hypothesis: positive imbalance -> continuation over next minutes; contrarian at extremes.
predictors.effect: Not in the original list. Equity/microstructure literature (Chordia-Roll-Subrahmanyam; Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov OFI) shows order-flow imbalance explains contemporaneous returns strongly and next-interval returns weakly; crypto studies (e.g., Silantyev 2019 'Order flow analysis of cryptocurrency markets', Digital Finance) report similar contemporaneous R^2 at minute horizons with predictive content decaying within minutes. No cost-adjusted evidence at the hourly/daily horizons the advisor would use. Could not be verified in this session.
predictors.oos_evidence: Microstructure results are largely in-sample regressions; no post-publication trading test at >5-minute horizons found.
predictors.costs_decay: Edge lives inside the bid-ask spread at sub-minute horizons; at 1h+ it is inside fees. Useful as a feature (flow regime, absorption vs. exhaustion), not as a signal.
predictors.data_source: Binance /futures/data/takerlongshortRatio (30-day window - archive), data.binance.vision aggTrades (full history), OKX rubik taker-volume, cryptofeed TRADES

predictors.name: [ADDED] Dealer gamma exposure / max-pain / option OI walls
predictors.formula: GEX_t = sum over strikes of OI * gamma * S^2 * 0.01 (sign by assumed dealer side); max pain = strike minimizing total option payout at expiry; 'pin' hypothesis: spot gravitates to max pain into large expiries; positive GEX dampens, negative GEX amplifies moves.
predictors.effect: Widely published by vendors (Deribit Insights, Greeks.live, Amberdata) but no peer-reviewed or pre-registered test for BTC found; equity evidence for expiration pinning exists (Ni-Pearson-Poteshman 2005) but is small and about clustering at strikes, not direction. Dealer-side sign is unobservable on Deribit (no OCC-style classification), so GEX sign is an assumption.
predictors.oos_evidence: None.
predictors.costs_decay: Unknown. At best a volatility-regime feature around expiries.
predictors.data_source: Deribit get_book_summary_by_currency, get_instruments (OI by strike), Laevitas, Amberdata

predictors.name: [ADDED] Spot BTC/ETH ETF net flows as positioning proxy
predictors.formula: Flow_t = sum of daily net creations/redemptions in USD across US spot ETFs (Farside/SoSoValue aggregation; T+1 publication); z-scored 5d/20d flow; hypothesis: flows lead returns.
predictors.effect: Only since Jan 2024 (~450 daily obs). Vendor analyses and my reading of 2024-2025 working papers suggest flows are mostly CONTEMPORANEOUS or lag returns (return-chasing), with little incremental next-day predictability; not verifiable here. Structural relevance is high because ETF/basis-trade demand now drives CME basis and Leveraged Fund COT shorts.
predictors.universe_period: US spot BTC ETFs 2024-01..; ETH ETFs 2024-07..
predictors.oos_evidence: None found; sample too short for regime-robust conclusions.

predictors.data_source: Farside Investors, SoSoValue, issuer daily holdings; CF Benchmarks basis for the hedge leg
