verdicts.name: Gradient-boosted trees on engineered features (G-Research / Jaquart / Akyildirim)
verdicts.note: gresearch.com, kaggle.com, sciencedirect.com and link.springer.com are all blocked by the egress proxy; WebSearch budget exhausted (200/200). Could not confirm the winning team name, that winners used LightGBM, the leaderboard metric value, Jaquart's per-horizon accuracies, or Akyildirim's 55-65%. The qAp repo confirms a Spacetimeformer entry (context 128/250, horizon 16) but reports no score, so 'transformers did not beat LightGBM' is also unconfirmed. Claims are consistent with my prior knowledge of these papers but nothing was checked at source this session. Strength downgraded moderate -> weak.

verdicts.name: Meta-labeling (Lopez de Prado / JFDS series)
verdicts.note: Confirmed via github.com/hudson-and-thames/meta-labeling: the four JFDS papers exist (Joubert Summer 2022; Meyer/Joubert/Alfeus Fall 2022; Thumm/Barucca/Joubert Winter 2022; Meyer/Barziy/Joubert Spring 2023) and the repo states meta-labeling helps 'size positions, filter out false-positive signals, and improve Sharpe and max drawdown' and that 'fixed position sizing methods is significantly improved by calibration'. NOT confirmed: whether data were synthetic vs real, any numbers, the Hudson & Thames two-strategy replication (hudsonthames.org blocked), and the 17%->63% figure. The original entry's claims about synthetic data and the base-rate artifact are plausible interpretations, not verified findings. Strength moderate -> weak (qualitative peer-reviewed support only, no crypto evidence).

verdicts.name: LSTM / RNN (Fischer-Krauss, Ghosh-Neufeld-Sahoo, Jaquart)
verdicts.note: EJOR (ScienceDirect), arXiv 2004.10178 (arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, huggingface papers, paperswithcode, econstor, scholar.archive.org) all blocked. The figures 0.46%/day, Sharpe 5.8, 1992-2015, post-2010 decay match my prior knowledge of Fischer & Krauss (2018) and Ghosh et al. (2022), but the '59.1% directional accuracy' attribution could not be checked and should not be quoted. Strength 'weak' stands; the cautionary decay narrative is the right lesson but is currently uncited-at-source.

verdicts.name: Transformers / attention models for crypto returns
verdicts.note: Only confirmed fact: qAp's Spacetimeformer solution used context 128 (train) / 250 (submit) and horizon 16; its README gives NO leaderboard score and NO LightGBM comparison. mlcontests.com blocked. arXiv 2608.05755 could not be opened (arXiv blocked) and its existence is unconfirmed. The statement 'transformers did not beat LightGBM' is inference, not evidence. Keep strength weak but note the negative claim is itself unverified.

verdicts.name: Regime-conditional models (NHHM, RS-CAViaR, MS-GARCH)
verdicts.note: arXiv 2011.03741, 2401.03393, 2107.05535 and both ScienceDirect articles blocked. Koki/Leonardos/Piliouras NHHM predictive-density claim matches prior knowledge but is unconfirmed; the key point that there is no directional/after-cost evidence remains true by absence. Strength moderate -> weak for direction; the entry should be reframed as 'use filtered posteriors as features' only.

verdicts.name: Ensembles and stacking
verdicts.note: Repo abstract confirms only 'ensembles are especially beneficial when underlying data consist of multiple regimes'. The quoted typical gain '+0.005-0.02 rank-corr' has no source; the claim that G-Research top teams averaged LightGBM seeds/folds is unverified (Kaggle blocked). Downgrade to weak; keep as engineering practice, not a predictor.

verdicts.name: Time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM, Kronos)
verdicts.note: Confirmed: TSFM_Finance repo = 'Re(visiting) Time Series Foundation Models in Finance' (Rahimikia, Ni, Wang; arXiv 2511.18578), tests Chronos 1.x and TimesFM 1.0/2.0; Kronos MIT, trained on K-lines from 45+ exchanges, authors say pipeline is 'not a production-ready quantitative trading system'; Chronos Apache-2.0, Chronos-2 released 2025-10-20. NOT confirmed this session: the ~50-51% accuracy, Chronos-large OOS R2 -1.37%, CatBoost Sharpe 6.79, Kronos Brier 0.189 vs 0.188 (cornfordandcross.com blocked), and the existence of arXiv 2606.27100 / 2609.20554. The repo's own prior research doc admits these were checked 'через GitHub/сниппеты'. The qualitative 'no directional edge' conclusion is consistent across what is accessible; strength no-evidence stands.

verdicts.name: Cross-sectional rank prediction (Numerai Crypto style)
verdicts.note: Confirmed from numerai/docs on GitHub: target = 30-day forward token return, ranked, gaussianized, bucketed into 5 bins; payout = stake*clip(payout_factor*mmc, -0.05, 0.05); CORR = Pearson on gaussianized ranks and centered target, both raised to power 1.5 with sign preserved; YIEDL community data = PVM, sentiment, on-chain. NOT confirmed: the quoted warning that basic-feature models 'will likely have no performance' (not on the data page fetched) and the 'CORR 0.02-0.04 is strong' lore. Strength weak stands.

verdicts.name: Cross-sectional crypto momentum / size factors (Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu)
verdicts.note: nber.org and semanticscholar blocked. Magnitudes and t-stats unconfirmed. The paper (J. Finance 2022) does exist per prior knowledge; the 'post-publication weakening' claim has no cited source. Strength weak stands; this belongs to a different family (cross-sectional factors) anyway.

verdicts.name: Validation design: purged/embargoed CPCV, DSR, PBO
verdicts.note: Confirmed at github.com/eslazarev/purged-cross-validation README: naive shuffled KFold R2 0.83 (k-NN) / 0.91 (RandomForest) on an unpredictable target vs -1.48 / -1.87 under PurgedKFold; train/test label overlap 100% -> 0%; MIT license. Kapoor & Narayanan (arXiv 2207.07048), arXiv 2410.14475 and the two SSRN papers could not be opened but are well-established. Strength strong stands.

corrected.family: ML models and ensembles for direction: what actually works out-of-sample (GBDT / RF / LSTM / transformers / meta-labeling / regime-conditional / stacking / competitions)
corrected.summary: Referee outcome: this session could verify at source only GitHub-hosted material (purgedcv demo, JFDS meta-labeling paper list, Numerai target/payout/CORR definitions, Kronos and Chronos licenses/disclaimers, qAp Spacetimeformer config, TSFM_Finance paper identity). Every journal/arXiv/Kaggle/NBER number in the previous draft is UNVERIFIED this session because arxiv.org, sciencedirect.com, link.springer.com, nber.org, ssrn, kaggle.com, gresearch.com, semanticscholar, huggingface, econstor and hudsonthames.org are blocked by the egress proxy and the WebSearch budget is exhausted. The qualitative conclusions survive and are consistent with prior knowledge, but strengths are downgraded: (1) The only item with 'strong' evidence is the validation methodology itself — naive CV manufactures skill (R2 0.83-0.91 on noise vs negative under purged CV, confirmed). (2) GBDT on engineered features is the sensible default, but the competition and paper numbers behind it (G-Research winner = LightGBM, Jaquart 1-60 min accuracies, Akyildirim 55-65%) could not be confirmed; treat 52-55% hit-rate on 4h-1d as a working hypothesis to be measured in-house, not a literature fact. (3) Meta-labeling has peer-reviewed qualitative support (four JFDS papers; improves Sharpe/MaxDD via filtering and sizing; calibration helps fixed sizers) but no crypto evidence and no verified numbers; the 17%->63% figure should not be quoted. (4) Regime-switching: no verified evidence of directional edge; use only filtered (causal) posteriors as GBDT features. (5) LSTM/transformers: no verified evidence they beat GBDT in crypto; the Fischer-Krauss decay story is the right lesson but its numbers are unverified here. (6) Foundation TS models: license facts confirmed, 'no edge' conclusion consistent, exact accuracies unverified. (7) Numerai Crypto definitions confirmed; it is a 30-day cross-sectional problem, not a BTC direction signal. Practical implication for the advisor: build the LightGBM/CatBoost + triple-barrier + purged CPCV + DSR/PBO pipeline and generate the evidence yourself; do not cite any literature accuracy figure to users until re-verified from a machine with open internet. Never promise returns.

predictors.name: Gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost) on engineered return/volume features
predictors.formula: y = sign(r_{t->t+h}) or triple-barrier label; X = lagged log returns at several lookbacks, realized vol, volume z-scores, high-low range, cross-asset returns, time-of-day. G-Research target (from memory, unverified): Target = r_{15min}(asset) - beta * r_{15min}(market), beta from rolling regression; metric = weighted Pearson corr(pred, Target).
predictors.horizon: 15 min (competition) to 1 day; expect most robust at 4h-1d
predictors.effect: UNVERIFIED this session: G-Research/Kaggle 2022 winner reportedly used LightGBM with hand-crafted features; leaderboard scores reportedly small positive correlations (order 0.01-0.05). Jaquart et al. (2021) reportedly >50% accuracy on BTC 1-60 min with GBC/LSTM best; Akyildirim et al. (2021) reportedly 55-65% on 12 cryptos but with non-purged splits. None of these numbers could be opened at source (Kaggle, gresearch.com, ScienceDirect, Springer all blocked). Working expectation to be measured in-house: 52-55% hit rate on 4h-1d, rank-IC 0.02-0.05.
predictors.oos_evidence: Competition holdout is the cleanest OOS design in crypto ML but its result could not be confirmed. No verified purged-CV replication of the academic accuracies exists in what was accessible.
predictors.universe_period: G-Research: 14 cryptos 2018-2022; Jaquart: BTC 2019-2020 minute data; Akyildirim: 12 cryptos 2013-2018 (all from memory)
predictors.costs_decay: Correlations of a few hundredths on 15-min residual returns are below 5-10 bp round-trip taker fees for single-asset trading; minute-level edges reportedly not exploitable after fees (Jaquart, unverified). Expect decay as market-making competition on BTC/ETH increased post-2021.
predictors.data_source: OHLCV via ccxt / data.binance.vision (already in repo); Kaggle dataset for replication (needs open internet).

predictors.name: Meta-labeling: secondary classifier on triple-barrier outcomes of a primary side signal
predictors.formula: Primary side s_t in {-1,+1}; triple-barrier label y_t = 1 if profit barrier (pt*sigma_t) hit before stop (sl*sigma_t) or vertical barrier h with sign matching s_t, else 0; M2(X_t, s_t) -> p_t; trade if p_t > tau; size = f(p_t) (fixed/calibrated sigmoid); sample weights = label uniqueness.
predictors.effect: CONFIRMED (hudson-and-thames/meta-labeling README): four JFDS papers (Joubert 2022; Meyer, Joubert & Alfeus 2022; Thumm, Barucca & Joubert 2022; Meyer, Barziy & Joubert 2023) state meta-labeling helps size positions, filter false positives and improve Sharpe and max drawdown; calibration 'significantly improved' fixed position-sizing methods while data-fitted sizers gained nothing; ensembles help most under multiple regimes. NOT confirmed: any numeric effect sizes, whether tests were synthetic or real, the Hudson & Thames two-strategy replication, and the 17%->63% figure (do not quote).
predictors.oos_evidence: Peer-reviewed but qualitative as far as could be verified; no crypto-specific OOS study accessible. Meta-labeling cannot create edge absent a primary signal (Joubert 2022 framing, from memory).
predictors.universe_period: Not verifiable this session (repo README gives abstracts only)
predictors.costs_decay: Filtering lowers trade count and thus cost drag; barrier widths must exceed ~2-3x round-trip cost or labels are noise.
predictors.data_source: Own OHLCV + primary signals (HMM/Elliott/rules) in repo; sigma from EWMA of returns.

predictors.name: LSTM / RNN on return sequences (Fischer-Krauss line)
predictors.formula: Input: sequence of 240 standardized daily log returns (or 60-240 minute returns); output P(r_{t+1} > cross-sectional median); trade top-k / bottom-k.
predictors.effect: UNVERIFIED this session (EJOR/arXiv/mirrors blocked). From memory: Fischer & Krauss (2018) S&P 500 1992-2015, ~0.46%/day and Sharpe ~5.8 before costs, edge fading after 2010; Ghosh, Neufeld & Sahoo (2022) intraday LSTM+RF confirm decay. The '59.1% directional accuracy' attribution could not be checked — drop it.
predictors.oos_evidence: The replicated lesson is post-publication decay; in crypto no accessible evidence that LSTM beats GBDT with identical features.
predictors.costs_decay: Equity edge reportedly ~zero after costs from 2010; minute-level crypto LSTM edges do not survive 5-10 bp fees.
predictors.data_source: OHLCV; for crypto ccxt/Binance vision.

predictors.name: Transformers / attention models (Spacetimeformer, PatchTST, iTransformer) for crypto returns
predictors.formula: Multivariate seq2seq; context 128 (train) / 250 (inference) bars across 14 assets; horizon 16 steps; MSE loss (qAp config, confirmed).
predictors.effect: CONFIRMED only that a Spacetimeformer entry existed with the above config; its README reports no score and no LightGBM comparison. The claim that transformers underperformed GBDT in G-Research is unverified (Kaggle/gresearch blocked). No accessible peer-reviewed crypto transformer study with purged CV and costs.
predictors.oos_evidence: None verifiable. Papers claiming >60% typically have leakage (overlapping windows, full-sample scaling) — general caution, not a checked finding.
predictors.costs_decay: Same as LSTM; high training cost and drift risk.
predictors.data_source: OHLCV; NeuralForecast only if it beats GBDT after costs on all CPCV paths.

predictors.name: Regime-conditional models: HMM / NHHM / Markov-switching as features
predictors.formula: S_t in {1..K}; r_t | S_t ~ N(mu_k, sigma_k^2); NHHM transition P(S_t=j|S_{t-1}=i, z_{t-1}) = logistic(z_{t-1}); feature = filtered posterior P(S_t=k | F_t) (forward filter only, never smoothed).
predictors.horizon: 1 day densities; as feature any horizon
predictors.effect: UNVERIFIED this session (arXiv 2011.03741, ScienceDirect, arXiv 2401.03393 blocked). From memory: Koki, Leonardos & Piliouras report best one-step predictive density for BTC/ETH/XRP with a 4-state NHHM; RS-CAViaR improves BTC VaR/ES. No evidence anywhere accessible of improved directional hit rate or after-cost returns from regimes alone.
predictors.oos_evidence: Density/tail-risk improvements reportedly rolling OOS; directional benefit: none verified. Smoothed posteriors are a look-ahead leak.
predictors.costs_decay: Slow-moving; value is in sizing/abstaining, not more signals.
predictors.data_source: Daily/4h returns; hmmlearn (in repo, limited maintenance), statsmodels MarkovAutoregression; forward filter only.

predictors.name: Ensembles and stacking (seed/fold averaging, DES, CPCV-OOF stacking)
predictors.formula: p_hat = sum_m w_m p_hat_m with w from OOS log-loss on purged folds (or simple mean); stacking meta-learner fit only on CPCV out-of-fold predictions.
predictors.effect: CONFIRMED only the JFDS abstract statement that ensembles are 'especially beneficial when underlying data consist of multiple regimes'. The '+0.005-0.02 rank-corr' figure and 'G-Research top teams averaged seeds' are unsourced — removed.
predictors.oos_evidence: Variance/PBO reduction is the plausible benefit; no verified signal gain.
predictors.costs_decay: Neutral; smoother probabilities reduce flip-flop trades.
predictors.data_source: Own models.

predictors.name: Time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM, Kronos) zero-shot on returns
predictors.formula: Zero-shot quantiles q_{0.1/0.5/0.9}(r_{t+1..t+H} | 512-2048 bar context); direction = sign(q_{0.5}); optionally quantile spread as a feature.
predictors.effect: CONFIRMED: 'Re(visiting) Time Series Foundation Models in Finance' (Rahimikia, Ni, Wang; arXiv 2511.18578; code DeepIntoStreams/TSFM_Finance) tests Chronos 1.x and TimesFM; Kronos is MIT, trained on K-lines from 45+ exchanges, and its authors call the demo 'not a production-ready quantitative trading system'; Chronos-2 Apache-2.0, released 2025-10-20. UNVERIFIED: ~50-51% directional accuracy, Chronos-large OOS R2 -1.37%, TimesFM-500M <50%, CatBoost in-sample Sharpe 6.79, Kronos Brier 0.189 vs 0.188 Brownian (cornfordandcross.com blocked); existence of arXiv 2606.27100 and 2609.20554 unconfirmed.
predictors.oos_evidence: Qualitative 'no directional edge' is consistent across what is accessible and with the repo's prior research doc, which itself notes these were checked only via GitHub/snippets.
predictors.costs_decay: No edge to decay; compute cost only. Evaluate only on bars after the model's pretraining cutoff.
predictors.data_source: Chronos-2 (Apache-2.0), TimesFM <=2.5 (Apache-2.0), Kronos (MIT).

predictors.name: Cross-sectional rank prediction (Numerai Crypto)
predictors.formula: CONFIRMED: target = 30-day forward token return, ranked, gaussianized, bucketed into 5 bins; CORR = Pearson(sign*|gauss(rank(pred))|^1.5, sign*|target-mean|^1.5); legacy payout = stake*clip(payout_factor*MMC, -0.05, 0.05).
predictors.effect: Numerai publishes no typical score magnitudes; 'CORR 0.02-0.04 is strong' is community lore (unverified). Only live staked submissions reveal skill.
predictors.oos_evidence: Live OOS by construction (black-box target).
predictors.costs_decay: Low turnover at 30d; not a BTC direction signal.
predictors.data_source: Numerai CryptoAPI (train_targets.parquet, live_universe.parquet); YIEDL community data (PVM, sentiment, on-chain), free.

predictors.name: Validation design as the gate on reported accuracy: purged/embargoed CPCV, DSR, PBO
predictors.formula: Purge overlapping label windows; embargo e bars after each test block; CPCV C(N,K) paths; PBO via CSCV; DSR = PSR at expected max Sharpe under N trials.
predictors.effect: CONFIRMED (purgedcv README): on an unpredictable target, shuffled KFold R2 = 0.83 (k-NN) / 0.91 (RandomForest); PurgedKFold R2 = -1.48 / -1.87; label overlap 100% -> 0%. MIT license.
predictors.oos_evidence: Methodological; Bailey & Lopez de Prado (DSR, PBO) are standard though SSRN was blocked this session.
predictors.costs_decay: Count every optuna trial / feature sweep / threshold in N for DSR; gate: DSR > 0.95, PBO < 0.2, positive after-cost expectancy on all CPCV paths.
predictors.data_source: purgedcv (MIT) or skfolio CombinatorialPurgedCV (BSD-3).

predictors.name: ADDED: Order-book / order-flow-imbalance deep models (DeepLOB, deep OFI) — where honest >55% accuracy exists but is not tradable for a Telegram bot
predictors.formula: Input: last T snapshots of L-level LOB (bid/ask price, size) or OFI_t = sum over levels of (delta bid size - delta ask size); CNN-LSTM (DeepLOB) or linear/GBDT; target = sign of mid-price change over next k events/seconds.
predictors.effect: UNVERIFIABLE this session (arXiv blocked). From memory: Zhang, Zohren & Roberts (2019) DeepLOB ~80%+ accuracy on FI-2010 and LSE at k=10-50 events; Kolm, Turiel & Westray (2023) deep OFI R2 of a few percent at short horizons. Effect is real in microstructure but decays to ~50% within minutes and is consumed by spread/fees for a taker.
predictors.oos_evidence: Chronological OOS in the papers; no verified crypto replication accessible.
predictors.costs_decay: Not monetizable via delayed Telegram signals; only for market-making / execution timing.
predictors.data_source: L2 snapshots via exchange websockets (must run from VPS/Mac — exchange APIs blocked from this container); data.binance.vision bookDepth.

predictors.name: ADDED: Probability calibration + abstention (conformal / MAPIE / crepes) as the layer that turns weak classifiers into usable signals
predictors.formula: Calibrate p_t (isotonic/Platt on purged OOF); conformal set at alpha; emit signal only if |p_t - 0.5| > tau AND conformal set is a singleton; expectancy_t = p_t*TP - (1-p_t)*SL - costs > 0.
predictors.effect: Mechanism, not a predictor: JFDS calibration paper (confirmed abstract) reports calibration significantly improves fixed sizers. No verified crypto numbers.
predictors.oos_evidence: Must be measured on CPCV paths with Brier/log-loss and reliability curves.
predictors.costs_decay: Abstention is the main after-cost lever for sparse single-asset signals.
predictors.data_source: MAPIE 1.5.0, crepes 0.9.1 (already noted in repo research doc).

red_flags: VERIFICATION STATUS: almost every numeric claim in this family is unverified at source this session (arXiv, ScienceDirect, Springer, NBER, SSRN, Kaggle, gresearch.com, Semantic Scholar, HuggingFace, econstor, alphaxiv, hudsonthames.org blocked; WebSearch 200/200 used). Only GitHub-hosted facts were confirmed. Re-verify from an unrestricted machine before quoting any accuracy figure to users.

The repo's own research doc (docs/research/regime-ai-stack-2026-09.md) states arXiv 2511.18578 and 2606.27100 were checked only 'через GitHub/сниппеты'; arXiv IDs 2606.27100, 2608.05755, 2609.20554 are unconfirmed to exist.

Reported crypto accuracies of 60-90% almost always come from price-level targets, shuffled splits with overlapping windows, full-sample scalers, smoothed (two-sided) regime labels, or test-set tuning. Akyildirim's 55-65% (unverified) reportedly used non-purged splits.
Hit rate is not expectancy: report after-cost expectancy per trade, Brier/log-loss and calibration, not accuracy.
Survivorship: today's top-N coin lists exclude dead tokens; use point-in-time universes.
Post-publication decay is the norm (Fischer-Krauss line, unverified numbers but consistent narrative); 2017-2021 crypto edges are likely smaller now.
Competition metrics (Pearson corr of a few hundredths, Numerai CORR) become money only via many netted bets at low cost; a single-asset BTC Telegram signal cannot harvest that.
Meta-labeling '17%->63%' should not be quoted; not found in any confirmed source and mechanically a base-rate shift.
Foundation TS models: no verified directional edge; also pretraining-cutoff look-ahead if evaluated on earlier data.
Multiple testing: count every optuna trial, feature set, barrier width and threshold in N for DSR.
Exchange APIs are blocked from this container — data collection and any replication must run from the VPS/Mac.

missing: Order-book / order-flow-imbalance deep models (DeepLOB, deep OFI) — the one setting with honest >55% directional accuracy, but only at tick-to-minute horizons and not monetizable via delayed Telegram signals (added, unverifiable this session).
Probability calibration + conformal abstention layer (MAPIE/crepes) as the mechanism that makes 52-55% classifiers usable after costs (added).

Cross-sectional ML on the coin panel (Gu-Kelly-Xiu-style GBDT/NN on many tokens with lagged returns, volume, on-chain) — e.g. Bianchi & Babiak style crypto return predictability studies; not verifiable this session, worth a dedicated check.

Concept-drift handling: rolling/expanding retrain schedules and drift tests (ADWIN, PSI on feature distributions) — no literature check possible here but operationally essential for any GBDT deployed on crypto.
Exact G-Research winning private-leaderboard correlation and the winning solution write-up (Kaggle discussion) — needed before citing the competition as evidence.
Independent purged-CV replications of Jaquart et al. and Akyildirim et al. on 2022-2026 data — none accessible; the project should produce its own.
